【最终交付（英文假设）】
Hypothesis: Within the interval 2000–1100 BCE, the highest growth phase is centered on the 15th century BCE (c. 1500–1401 BCE, the "1500s"), with strong growth continuing through the 14th century BCE (c. 1400–1301 BCE, the "1400s"). Three independent proxies converge on this. (1) Archaeological activity: the mean annual KDE growth rate g_all_mean is highest in the 1500s block (mean ≈ +0.0028/yr, median +0.0029, 100% of years positive; the top-growth years 1432–1452 BCE all fall in the 15th century), followed by the 1400s (+0.0015/yr, 100% positive), whereas the 13th (−0.0016) and 12th (−0.0044) centuries BCE are negative. (2) Landscape/population proxy (pollen openness): the 100-yr smoothed openness rises most strongly in the 1500s (+≈0.98 level units, ≈ +2.6%/yr), continues in the 1400s (+0.66), recovering from a clear trough after the 16th-century BCE decline (−1.65). (3) Material wealth (four capitals with the approved mapping): the single largest century-scale gain across symbolic, social and economic capital occurs between the 1500 and 1400 BCE markers (total mean column-delta ≈ +2.6), driven chiefly by social capital (copper/gold, amber, monuments: +1.53) and symbolic capital (axes/swords, daggers, house size: +0.75), and wealth levels peak at the 1400 BCE marker and stay high at 1300 BCE. Both binning conventions (9 full-century blocks and 10 discrete century points) agree: fastest growth = 1500s BCE (scheme B top interval 1500→1400 BCE), second = 1400s BCE (1400→1300 BCE). The growth phase is bracketed by the 16th-century BCE decline on one side and a 13th–12th century BCE downturn on the other. Caveats: raw pollen readings cover only ~5% of this interval, so the openness signal is interpolation/smoothing-sensitive; pollen_grate_100 cannot be reproduced from the data and is used only as low-confidence corroboration (directionally it also ranks 1500s then 1400s); the level/wealth peak sits at the 1400 BCE marker, so the exact peak has a ±1-century edge between growth-rate (15th c BCE) and accumulated-level (14th c BCE) definitions.

payload.hypothesis: The highest growth phase within 2000-1100 BCE is centered on the 15th century BCE (c. 1500-1401 BCE), with strong growth continuing through the 14th century BCE (c. 1400-1301 BCE). This is supported by three independent proxies: (1) the archaeological KDE growth rate g_all_mean peaks in the 1500s (+0.0028/yr mean, 100% positive years; top years 1432-1452 BCE) with the 1400s second (+0.0015/yr) versus negative 13th-12th centuries BCE; (2) pollen openness (100-yr smoothed) rises most strongly in the 1500s (+0.98 level, ~+2.6%/yr) and 1400s (+0.66), recovering from a 16th-century BCE trough (-1.65); (3) the four capitals (approved mapping) show the largest century gain between the 1500 and 1400 BCE markers (total mean column-delta +2.6, chiefly social +1.53 and symbolic +0.75), with wealth levels peaking at the 1400 BCE marker. Both binning schemes agree; the growth phase is bounded by the 16th-century decline and the 13th-12th century downturn.
payload.workflow: 1) Load and clean three CSV files (capital and pollen columns use comma decimals; CE=-BCE, calBP=1950-CE verified). 2) Restrict to CE in [-2000,-1100] (901 gap-free annual points; capital has 10 discrete century markers). 3) Build century blocks by CE-flooring (Scheme A: 9 full centuries 2000s..1200s + endpoint year 1100 BCE), and Scheme B: 10 discrete points (intervals between consecutive markers). 4) Compute per-century growth proxies: mean g_all_mean (KDE growth rate), self-computed pollen-openness growth (pollen_inter / pollen_inter_100 rolling-100 means), and capital century deltas grouped into Symbolic/Social/Economic/Cultural with the approved column mapping. 5) Rank centuries per proxy, cross-validate (Spearman), and check scheme A vs B agreement; flag pollen_grate_100 as low-confidence (definition not reproducible). 6) Synthesize the highest-growth centuries and write the data-grounded English hypothesis with stated caveats.
